title: Checkout failures after the payment SDK upgrade

sections.summary: Between 09:10 and 10:05 on 12 November, one in five checkout attempts failed with a timeout. The payment SDK upgraded the day before opened a new connection for every request, which exhausted the connection pool. Rolling back the SDK stopped the failures; a pinned pool size and a load test now guard the upgrade.
sections.symptoms:
- Customers saw "Payment could not be completed" after about 30 seconds.
- The checkout error rate alert fired at 09:14.
- Support received 42 tickets in the first hour.
sections.impact:
| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Failed checkouts | 1,870 |
| Duration | 55 minutes |
| Customers affected | about 1,400 |
sections.timeline:
| Time (UTC+7) | Event |
|---|---|
| 11 Nov 17:30 | Payment SDK 4.2 deployed |
| 12 Nov 09:10 | First timeouts in the checkout service |
| 09:14 | Error rate alert fires |
| 09:40 | Connection pool exhaustion found |
| 10:05 | SDK rolled back to 4.1; errors stop |
sections.root-cause:
SDK 4.2 creates a new HTTP client per call unless a shared client is passed in. Under morning traffic each checkout held a connection until the gateway timeout, so the pool of 200 connections ran out.

Ruled out: the gateway itself (its own latency stayed normal) and the database (no slow queries).
sections.evidence:
- Pool metrics: active connections reached 200 at 09:09 and stayed there.
- Release notes of SDK 4.2: "clients are no longer shared by default".
- `CheckoutService.pay()` builds the SDK without a client.
sections.fix: The SDK was rolled back to 4.1 at 10:05. The upgrade was redone with a shared client and verified with a load test of twice the morning peak.
sections.prevention:
- Pin the pool size and alert at 80 % use (owner: platform team).
- Add the load test to the release checklist of payment changes (owner: checkout team).
sections.open-questions: - Should the gateway timeout be shortened from 30 to 10 seconds?
